note: Loot sources whose real mechanic is not visible in their drop rows. A watchlisted source fails the not_on_watchlist validation check and is forced to needs_review however cleanly it parses, because parsing cleanly proves nothing about a mechanic the rows do not encode. Remove an entry only when the mechanic is modelled and the simulation has been checked against the wiki's own figures.

entries.title: Lunar Chest
entries.detail: Uniques are drawn without replacement across the chest's rolls, so the same unique cannot come up twice in one chest. The drop rows carry per-item rarities only and cannot express that. Model as a weighted table with rolls > 1 and withoutReplacement: true.

entries.title: Reward Cart
entries.detail: Rolls scale with points earned during the activity rather than being a fixed count per kill. The rows give per-item rarities within one roll and say nothing about how many rolls a run yields. Needs the tempoross_points formula.

entries.title: Reward pool
entries.detail: Rolls scale with points earned during the activity rather than being a fixed count per kill. Needs the wintertodt_points formula.

entries.title: Duke Sucellus
entries.detail: Loot is a sequential roll-until-success chain described only in page prose, not in any drop row: 1/90 tradeable unique table (1/30 awakened), else 1/48 awakener's orb, else 1/25 frozen tablet, else 1/200 ice quartz, else 1/5 supply drop table, else the standard table; separately 1/2500 Baron and 1/40 clue after that. A perfect kill also gives 50% more loot from the standard table. The page's dropsline rows reconcile to a valid denominator on their own, so this source parses cleanly and would otherwise look verified — the chain order and the perfect-kill bonus are the parts that are invisible to the parser.

entries.title: Zalcano
entries.detail: Both the main table and the tertiary table scale with points from damage dealt to Zalcano's hitpoints and shield (points formula and per-component caps are in page prose, not in any drop row), and the MVP gets an extra 10% of their non-unique loot. The page's dropsline rows reconcile on their own, so this source parses cleanly and would otherwise look verified.

entries.title: Chest (Tombs of Amascut)
entries.detail: Unique chance scales with raid invocation level and completion points, not with any fixed per-kill rarity — needs the toa_invocation formula. The chest's own dropsline rows are structural leftovers of the raid's point-purchase reward shop, not independent per-row rarities; parsing them as an ordinary weighted table would misrepresent the mechanic entirely regardless of whether the weights happen to reconcile.

entries.title: Monumental chest
entries.detail: Unique chance scales with Theatre of Blood points earned across the raid (raid tier, deaths, personal performance), not a fixed per-kill rarity — needs the tob_points formula. Same caveat as the Tombs of Amascut chest: the dropsline rows reflect the points-shop structure, not independent rarities.

entries.title: Rewards Chest (Fortis Colosseum)
entries.detail: Loot scales with how many of the Colosseum's 12 waves were completed before the chest was opened (partial completion is allowed and bankable between waves), not with a fixed per-kill rarity. No formula for this is in PROJECT_PLAN.md's section 4.6 registry yet — it needs a new one (wave count / invocation-style scaling), not one of the seven already listed.

entries.title: Abyssal Sire
entries.detail: The wiki's own {{RareDropTable|3/139|...|multiplier=2}} call states this monster always drops DOUBLE the usual quantity from the rare drop table. The parser reads the 3/139 access rate correctly (tableRef to rare_drop_table resolves and parses cleanly) but the x2 quantity multiplier is not modelled — data/tables/rare_drop_table.json is one shared, unscaled record and nothing lets a per-boss tableRef access scale its yield.

entries.title: Corporeal Beast
entries.detail: The wiki's own {{GemDropTable|12/512|rolls=10|override=...}} call explicitly states in its override prose: "a 12/512 chance of rolling the gem drop table, whereupon its contents are rolled 10 times" — access checked ONCE, the gem table drawn 10 times after. The parser's default reading of `rolls` (used for every other RDT/gem access line on the wiki, matching Table.rolls' existing 'repeated access attempts' meaning elsewhere, e.g. Zulrah's main table) is the OPPOSITE: it currently models this as 10 independent 12/512 access attempts, not one access followed by 10 draws. Confirmed wrong specifically by this source's own text, not a guess — see docs/DECISIONS.md.
